name: Strange Set
description: Note that the memory limit is unusual. You are given an integer $$$n$$$ and two sequences $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ and $$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$$$. Let's call a set of integers $$$S$$$ such that $$$S \subseteq \{1, 2, 3, \dots, n\}$$$ strange , if, for every element $$$i$$$ of $$$S$$$, the following condition is met: for every $$$j \in [1, i - 1]$$$, if $$$a_j$$$ divides $$$a_i$$$, then $$$j$$$ is also included in $$$S$$$. An empty set is always strange . The cost of the set $$$S$$$ is $$$\sum\limits_{i \in S} b_i$$$. You have to calculate the maximum possible cost of a strange set.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3000$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 100$$$). The third line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$$$ ($$$-10^5 \le b_i \le 10^5$$$).
output_specification: Print one integer — the maximum cost of a strange set.
approach_summary: Model constraint matching as minimum-cost flow. Augment along the shortest augmenting path using SPFA or Dijkstra with Johnson's potentials.
